v.why: Stacked 3x3 convs give diminishing receptive-field returns, especially on 16x16 ImageNet16-120.
A 3x3 after a 3x3 is partially substitutive and saturates.
Deep stacks of 3x3 along the longest chain add little and make optimization harder.
A weakened feeder into node 2 leaves edge 5 with less signal to exploit, so its upgrade gains less.
With edge 0 absent, node 1 is dead, so changing edge 2 has almost no effect.
With edge 0 absent, node 1 gets no input, so edge 4 carries nothing and its op change has almost no effect.
The interior edge 2 is largely redundant when the direct edge is already a 3x3 conv.
Filling an empty final edge with even a parameter-free op adds a path, which beats replacing an existing op.
Adding a free identity path on an empty direct edge gains more than replacing any existing op, which would lose capacity.
A skip on an absent interior edge adds a gradient path, while replacing a conv would lose capacity.
